solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Warning from victim pierced by arrow perhaps (10)

indicators.note: PREY is pierced, so CURSOR goes inside it

blocks.note: the on-screen arrow is one kind of cursor

annotation.surface: Someone shot with an arrow cries out a warning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arrow perhaps' pulls toward archery, but it is the pointer on a computer screen.
annotation.definitionFit: A precursory sign comes before and warns of what follows, so it is a warning sign.

entries.clue: Language used by Chopin buff (6)

blocks.note: the verb: to buff is to rub a surface until it shines

annotation.surface: A devoted fan of Chopin speaks a particular language.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buff' reads as an enthusiast, a Chopin buff, but it is the verb meaning to shine.
annotation.definitionFit: Chopin was born in Poland and spoke Polish.

entries.clue: Drink for one girlfriend on edge (3-4)

blocks.note: the lip of a cup is its edge

annotation.surface: A nervous girlfriend needs a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For one' is the setters' way of saying 'for example', giving EG.
annotation.definitionFit: An egg-flip is a drink of beer or spirits beaten up with egg and sugar.

entries.clue: Gypsy wedding welcomes group of sisters most of all (14)

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so UNION takes CONVENT inside it
take ALL without its last letter

annotation.surface: A Gypsy wedding is attended by a party of nuns.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most of all' sounds like 'above everything' but is just ALL losing a letter. 'Gypsy' used as an adjective means bohemian.
annotation.definitionFit: Gypsy in the sense of a roving, bohemian life means unconventional.

entries.clue: Work out one divided by five (5)

indicators.note: SOLE is split in two with V between the halves

annotation.surface: A sum: work out one divided by five.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue poses as arithmetic; 'divided by' means split by an inserted letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: working out a puzzle or sum means finding its answer.

entries.clue: Two bones carrying some RNA particles (9)

indicators.note: OS carries SOME inside it

blocks.note: the second: os is Latin for bone
taken as it stands, inside OS

annotation.surface: Two bones are found to hold some RNA particles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a vague quantity for the RNA but is lifted whole into OS.
annotation.definitionFit: Ribosomes are the tiny particles of RNA and protein where cells build proteins.

entries.clue: Son with a black mop (4)

annotation.surface: A boy with a mop of black hair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black mop' paints a head of hair; the mop is the cleaning kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A swab is a mop, especially for a ship's deck.

entries.clue: Dams to protect the same odd fish (7)

indicators.note: WEIRS surround and protect DO

blocks.note: a weir is a low river dam

annotation.surface: River dams built to protect a strange species of fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd fish' is a person, not a fish: a strange character. DO is ditto, the same again.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'odd fish' is British slang for a strange person, and the plural matches.

entries.clue: Novice’s secret desire to lead (8)

indicators.note: BEG goes in front of INNER

blocks.note: to beg is to ask for what one desires

annotation.surface: A newcomer privately longs to be in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a character sketch, the eager novice; 'to lead' only puts BEG first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a novice is someone new to a skill, just starting out.

entries.clue: Robin or Doris to be chosen in time (3,2,5,4)

definitions.text: Robin or Doris to be chosen

blocks.clueFragment: Robin or Doris to be chosen
blocks.note: the two share a famous surname; choose between the pair

annotation.surface: Someone named Robin or Doris will be selected in due course.
annotation.walkthrough: Robin Day was a famous British TV political interviewer and Doris Day the American singer and actress: two Days, so choose one of these Days.
annotation.definitionFit: One of these days means at some point in the future, in time.

entries.clue: Sound of American serving in bar (7)

indicators.note: the GI serves inside LOCAL

blocks.note: your local is your nearest pub
a GI is a US soldier, an American in service

annotation.surface: An American working behind the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is not noise but sensible reasoning. A local is a British neighbourhood pub.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of reasoning: a sound argument holds together step by step.

entries.clue: Financial people into crack (7)

definitions.note: BANKING is a noun used like an adjective, as in 'banking sector' for 'financial sector'

indicators.note: 'into' literally means entering, so the people go inside the crack's sound

blocks.note: a crack of noise, a bang

annotation.surface: People in finance who are into crack cocaine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests drugs; it is the sound, a bang.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun used attributively: the trade of banks stands for finance generally, as in a financial or banking crisis.

entries.clue: Peace slogan involving diligence, no less (7,2,6)

indicators.note: to involve is literally to roll up or entangle, so the letters get tangled

annotation.surface: A campaign slogan for peace that demands hard work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peace' here is quiet, not the end of war, so the slogan is a proverb praising silence.
annotation.definitionFit: Silence is golden is a saying in praise of peace and quiet.

entries.clue: Niche software, I’d say (4)

indicators.note: what I'd say is what is spoken

annotation.surface: An opinion that some software is niche.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Niche software' reads as specialist programs; the niche is the curved recess in a church.
annotation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess, a niche, especially at the east end of a church.

entries.clue: Coffee cup taken back in the end (9)

indicators.note: 'taken back' means returned, so the word for taken goes back the way it came, right to left
the result goes in DEMISE

blocks.note: an exam is taken or sat

annotation.surface: A coffee cup is returned when you finish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the end' looks like 'eventually' but is two jobs: 'in' places the piece, 'the end' is DEMISE.
annotation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup for strong black coffee.

entries.clue: Was about to be sorted (5,4)

annotation.surface: Something was just about to be sorted out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was about to' reads as 'nearly'; split it after 'about' to see 'was about', meaning concerned.
annotation.definitionFit: A report that dealt with a subject was about it; a problem dealt with is sorted.

entries.clue: Heartless lad splits from disabled ex (3,5)

indicators.note: LAD loses its middle letter
to split something is to break it in two, so the lad's letters wedge between O and F

blocks.note: of means from, as in 'of noble birth'

annotation.surface: A heartless boy breaks up with his disabled former partner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a link word between 'splits' and 'disabled' but supplies OF.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a flame is a lover, and an old one is a former partner.

entries.clue: Meadow — wide opening remains, however (9)

indicators.note: W opens up STAYS and sits inside

blocks.note: W is a wide in cricket scoring, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach

annotation.surface: A meadow with a wide gap in it is still there, however.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wide opening' suggests a first letter, but W is the cricket abbreviation, and 'opening' says it opens STAYS.
annotation.definitionFit: Leastways is a dialect word meaning at least, however.

entries.clue: Generally free (2,5)

blocks.note: on the loose, of an escaped prisoner

annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, 'generally free'; split them and each is a sense of AT LARGE.
annotation.definitionFit: At large means in general and also not captured.

entries.clue: Former morning paper (4)

blocks.note: an ex is a former one

annotation.surface: Yesterday's morning newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Morning paper' paints a newspaper; the paper is an exam paper.
annotation.definitionFit: An exam paper is often just called a paper.

entries.clue: Old car restricted by minimal leg room (7)

indicators.note: the answer is held within the following words

annotation.surface: An old car cramped by having very little leg room.
annotation.walkthrough: The Austin Allegro was a British family car of the 1970s, not a musical tempo here.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Austin model was built from 1973 to 1982, so 'old' dates it.

entries.clue: See 26
Radical thought about poor weaver (6,9)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the word for thought goes around the word for poor

blocks.note: I felt that = I thought that
to ravel is to tangle or weave threads

annotation.surface: A radical idea concerning an impoverished weaver.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Radical thought' reads as a bold idea; 'Radical' alone is the definition, a noun for a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A fellow traveller is a sympathiser with a radical cause, especially communism.

entries.clue: Capital account, one without credit (5)

indicators.note: A stands outside CR, after it

annotation.surface: A capital account with someone who has no credit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital account' is a banking term; the capital is a city.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the city is the capital of Ghana, one capital among many.

entries.clue: See departing aviatrix recklessly flying vehicle (3,4)

indicators.note: something departing leaves, so the letter for 'see' goes out of the word
the remaining letters are rearranged wildly

blocks.note: v. is vide, Latin for see

annotation.surface: Watch a woman pilot leave, flying her vehicle recklessly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recklessly flying' seems to belong together; 'recklessly' is the anagram signal and 'flying' belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An air taxi is a small plane hired for short trips.

entries.clue: Rough, cold and in tatters (7)

annotation.surface: A description of a vagrant: rough, cold and in rags.
annotation.walkthrough: The three words look like a list of hardships; the first is the definition and the rest is wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Cragged means rugged, rough like a crag.

entries.clue: Still happening? Not quite (4)

indicators.note: not quite all of the word: it stops one letter short

blocks.note: an event is a happening; drop the last letter

annotation.surface: A question whether something is still going on, with a hesitant answer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still happening?' reads as asking if something continues; 'Still' is the definition, as in 'still better' = 'even better'.
annotation.definitionFit: Still and even both intensify a comparison: still more, even more.

entries.clue: & 20: One finds resistance better when a dog is barking (10)

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A claim that a dog's barking helps someone find the strength to resist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' sounds like defiance but is electrical; barking is British slang for mad, a standard anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A Wheatstone bridge is a circuit used to measure an unknown electrical resistance.
